q: A bidder is a start-up recognised by DIPP and submits a bid for a works tender under GCC for Works after ACS No. 11. The tender document demands full Bid Security from every bidder without exception. What is the correct treatment for this bidder?

options.A: It must deposit Bid Security at 2% like any other bidder
options.B: It is exempt from depositing Bid Security
options.C: It must deposit 50% of the Bid Security
options.D: It must deposit Bid Security at 5% as Performance Guarantee

e: DIPP-recognised start-ups are exempt from Bid Security under ACS No. 11.

q: A Labour Co-operative Society is the lowest bidder for a work whose Bid Security, computed at the standard rate, works out to Rs 1,80,000. How much Bid Security must the Society actually deposit?
e: Labour Co-operative Societies deposit only 50% of the Bid Security.

q: After award of a contract priced at Rs 6 crore, the contractor proposes to sub-contract work worth Rs 3.30 crore to another agency. Under ACS No. 11, this proposal is:

options.A: Permissible, as sub-contracting has no ceiling
options.B: Permissible, as it is below 60% of the contract price
options.C: Not permissible, as sub-contracting is capped at 40% of the contract price
options.D: Permissible only if the sub-contractor deposits Additional PG

e: Sub-contracting is limited to a maximum of 40% of the contract price; Rs 3.30 crore is 55% of Rs 6 crore.

q: A tender is finalised at 8% below the advertised value. The contractor has furnished the normal Performance Guarantee. What additional security, if any, is required under ACS No. 11?
e: Additional PG of 5% applies only where the bid is more than 5% below the advertised value; 8% crosses that limit.

q: A contractor quotes 3% below the advertised value and the bid is accepted. The executive insists on collecting Additional Performance Guarantee. The correct position under ACS No. 11 is:

options.A: Bid Security must be doubled instead
options.B: Additional PG of 5% must be collected
options.C: Additional PG of 3% must be collected
options.D: No additional security is payable for a bid 0% to 5% below the advertised value

e: For bids 0% to 5% below the advertised value, no additional security is taken under ACS No. 11.

q: LOA was issued on 1 April. The contractor furnishes the Performance Guarantee on the 30th day. For the delay, penal interest under the GCC will be charged:

options.A: At 12% from the first day after LOA
options.D: No interest, as PG was furnished within 60 days

e: PG is due within 21 days; delay attracts 12% penal interest from the 22nd day onwards.

q: A contractor fails to furnish the Performance Guarantee even 65 days after the date of LOA, despite reminders. Under the GCC after ACS No. 11, the contract is liable to:

options.A: Extension of time without any penalty
options.C: Termination after 60 days from the date of LOA
options.D: Automatic conversion into a limited tender

e: PG default leads to termination after 60 days from the date of LOA.

q: A works tender valued at Rs 14 crore is processed under the two-packet system. What minimum tender validity must be stipulated?
e: Validity for two-packet tendering is 90 days; two-packet applies to tenders above Rs 10 crore.

q:
Consider the following statements about Bid Security after ACS No. 11:
1. Bid Security is the new name for EMD.
2. It is charged at a flat 2% of the estimated cost for all works.
3. It is rounded off to the nearest Rs 100.
4. It varies slab-wise with the value of the work.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
e: ACS No. 11 fixes Bid Security at a flat 2% for all works, rounded to the nearest Rs 100; there is no slab variation.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Start-ups recognised by DIPP are exempt from Bid Security.
2. Labour Co-operative Societies deposit the full Bid Security.
3. Labour Co-operative Societies deposit 50% of the Bid Security.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: DIPP-recognised start-ups are exempt; Labour Co-operative Societies deposit 50%, not the full amount.

q:
Consider the following statements about Performance Guarantee:
1. PG is 5% and is to be submitted within 21 days.
2. Delayed PG attracts penal interest at 12% from the 22nd day.
3. PG default can lead to termination after 60 days from LOA.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
e: All three statements state the PG position after ACS No. 11 correctly.

q:
Consider the following statements about Additional Performance Guarantee (APG):
1. No APG is taken where the bid is 4% below the advertised value.
2. APG of 5% is taken where the bid is more than 5% below the advertised value.
3. APG of 5% is taken for every accepted bid, whatever the discount.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
e: APG applies only beyond 5% below the advertised value; it is not payable on every bid.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Bid Capacity eligibility threshold has been reduced from Rs 20 crore to Rs 10 crore.
2. The Bid Capacity threshold has been raised from Rs 10 crore to Rs 20 crore.
3. ACS No. 11 is dated 13.03.2026.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
e: ACS No. 11 dt 13.03.2026 reduced the threshold from Rs 20 crore to Rs 10 crore, not the reverse.

q:
Consider the following statements about tender validity:
1. The minimum tender validity is 60 days.
2. In two-packet tendering, the validity is 90 days.
3. In two-packet tendering, the validity is 60 days.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
e: Ordinary minimum validity is 60 days; two-packet validity is 90 days.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The two-packet system applies to tenders valuing more than Rs 10 crore.
2. Tendering is done through IREPS.
3. The GCC for Works is issued by the Civil Engineering Directorate.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
e: All three are star points of the GCC position: two-packet above Rs 10 crore, IREPS tendering, GCC issued by the Civil Engineering Directorate.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. e-Reverse Auction applies for tenders of Rs 50 crore and above.
2. Sub-contracting is capped at 40% of the contract price.
3. Sub-contracting is capped at 50% of the contract price.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
e: e-Reverse Auction applies at Rs 50 crore and above, and the sub-contracting cap is 40%, not 50%.

q:
Consider the following statements about ACS No. 11:
1. It amends the GCC for Works, April 2022.
2. It was issued vide Board letter No. 2022/CE-I/CT/GCC-2022/Policy/Pt.I.
3. It raised Bid Security slab-wise for larger works.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
e: ACS No. 11 dt 13.03.2026 amends GCC April 2022 under the cited Board letter; Bid Security became flat 2%, not slab-wise.

q: Under ACS No. 11 to the GCC for Works, Bid Security is charged at what rate?

options.B: 2% of the estimated cost of the work
options.D: 2% of the contract value, without rounding

e: Bid Security is a flat 2% of the estimated cost for all works, rounded to the nearest Rs 100.

q: The GCC for Works is issued by which directorate?
e: The GCC is issued by the Civil Engineering Directorate.

q: e-Reverse Auction under the GCC framework applies to tenders of what value?
e: e-Reverse Auction applies for tenders of Rs 50 crore and above.

q: What is the rate of Performance Guarantee under the GCC for Works?
e: Performance Guarantee is 5%, to be submitted within 21 days.

q: Tendering for works under the GCC is done through which portal?
e: Tendering is done through IREPS.

q: The estimated cost of a work is Rs 2,50,00,000. What is the Bid Security payable by an ordinary bidder under ACS No. 11?
e: Bid Security is 2% of the estimated cost.

q: The estimated cost of a work is Rs 73,40,000. A Labour Co-operative Society bids for the work. What Bid Security must it deposit under ACS No. 11?
e: Standard Bid Security is 2% of estimated cost; the Society deposits 50% of that amount.

q: The contract price of a work is Rs 8,00,00,000. What is the maximum value of work that can be sub-contracted under ACS No. 11?
e: Sub-contracting is capped at 40% of the contract price.

q: Which of the following statements about Bid Security after ACS No. 11 is NOT correct?

options.A: It is charged at a flat 2% of the estimated cost for all works
options.B: It is rounded off to the nearest Rs 100
options.C: DIPP-recognised start-ups are exempt from it
options.D: It is charged slab-wise, rising with the value of the work

e: The slab-wise position is not correct; ACS No. 11 prescribes a flat 2% for all works.

q: Which of the following statements about Performance Guarantee is NOT correct?

options.A: PG is 5%, to be submitted within 21 days
options.B: Penal interest at 12% runs from the 22nd day for delayed PG
options.C: Additional PG of 5% is payable even where the bid is 2% below the advertised value
options.D: PG default can lead to termination after 60 days from LOA

e: No APG is payable for a bid only 2% below the advertised value; APG applies only beyond 5% below.

q: Which of the following statements about tender validity and the two-packet system is NOT correct?

options.A: Two-packet system applies to all tenders above Rs 1 crore
options.C: Validity in two-packet tendering is 90 days
options.D: Two-packet system applies to tenders above Rs 10 crore

e: Two-packet applies only above Rs 10 crore, not above Rs 1 crore.

q: Which of the following about ACS No. 11 is NOT correct?

options.A: Sub-contracting was capped at 40% of the contract price
options.B: Bid Capacity threshold was raised from Rs 10 crore to Rs 20 crore
options.C: Bid Security was fixed at 2% of the estimated cost
options.D: Bid Capacity threshold was reduced from Rs 20 crore to Rs 10 crore

e: The threshold was reduced, not raised; statement C reverses the change.

q: Which of the following statements about tendering portals, the GCC and Bid Security concessions is NOT correct?

options.B: The GCC is issued by the Civil Engineering Directorate
options.C: e-Reverse Auction applies at Rs 50 crore and above
options.D: Labour Co-operative Societies are fully exempt from Bid Security

e: Labour Co-operative Societies deposit 50% of Bid Security; only DIPP-recognised start-ups are exempt.

q:
Assertion (A): A DIPP-recognised start-up need not deposit Bid Security for a works tender.
Reason (R): ACS No. 11 exempts start-ups recognised by DIPP from Bid Security.

options.A: Both A and R are true and R correctly explains A
options.B: Both A and R are true but R does not explain A
options.C: A is true but R is false
options.D: A is false but R is true

e: The exemption in the Reason is exactly why the Assertion holds.

q:
Assertion (A): Additional PG is payable where the accepted bid is 4% below the advertised value.
Reason (R): Additional PG of 5% applies only where the bid is more than 5% below the advertised value.

options.A: Both A and R are true and R correctly explains A
options.B: Both A and R are true but R does not explain A
options.C: A is true but R is false
options.D: A is false but R is true

e: A is false because 4% is within the no-APG band; R correctly states the rule.

q:
Assertion (A): The Bid Capacity eligibility threshold now stands at Rs 10 crore.
Reason (R): ACS No. 11 reduced the threshold from Rs 20 crore to Rs 10 crore.

options.A: Both A and R are true and R correctly explains A
options.B: Both A and R are true but R does not explain A
options.C: A is true but R is false
options.D: A is false but R is true

e: The reduction stated in R is the direct cause of the present threshold in A.

q:
Assertion (A): In two-packet tendering, the minimum validity is 90 days.
Reason (R): The two-packet system applies to tenders valuing more than Rs 10 crore.

options.A: Both A and R are true and R correctly explains A
options.B: Both A and R are true but R does not explain A
options.C: A is true but R is false
options.D: A is false but R is true

e: Both statements are true, but the applicability threshold in R does not by itself explain the 90-day validity period.

q:
Assertion (A): Penal interest for delayed PG is charged from the date of LOA itself.
Reason (R): Penal interest at 12% is charged from the 22nd day onwards.

options.A: Both A and R are true and R correctly explains A
options.B: Both A and R are true but R does not explain A
options.C: A is true but R is false
options.D: A is false but R is true

e: A is false; interest starts only from the 22nd day, as R correctly states.
